headline.text: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta testified to NYC Council. Musk's SpaceXAI skipped it.

slides.altText: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta testified to NYC Council. Musk's SpaceXAI skipped it.

headline.text: Musk's SpaceXAI did not show up

slides.altText: Musk's SpaceXAI did not show up

body.text: SpaceXAI was the only company called that did not attend. Council Speaker Julie Menin says that violates its subpoena, a legal order compelling attendance and sworn testimony, and the Council will pursue it in court.

headline.text: Three firms agreed after a subpoena threat, Council says

slides.altText: Three firms agreed after a subpoena threat, Council says

body.text: Menin's office says Google and Anthropic declined by the Sept 25 deadline. OpenAI and Google agreed Sept 27, and Anthropic confirmed late that night, hours before a subpoena was due to be served. Meta had agreed.

headline.text: None of the four sent a CEO

slides.altText: None of the four sent a CEO

body.text: Anthropic: Logan Graham, head of its Frontier Red Team. OpenAI: Morgan Dwyer, head of policy development and operations. Google: Alice Friend. Meta: Shane Cahill, AI policy director for legislation.

headline.text: Menin opened by criticising Washington's light touch

slides.altText: Menin opened by criticising Washington's light touch

body.text: The hearing was a rare Committee of the Whole, which convenes all 51 Council members. Menin opened by criticising the federal light-touch approach, after President Trump signed a voluntary accord with tech leaders last week.

headline.text: Two former lab researchers urged caution

slides.altText: Two former lab researchers urged caution

body.text: Jacob Coxon, who quit Anthropic last month, called the industry's approach extremely reckless. Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo called for more transparency and for slowing development of the leading models.

headline.text: Misaligned AI could be more dangerous than China

headline.text: Proposed fine: $25,000 for breaking either of two AI laws

slides.altText: Proposed fine: $25,000 for breaking either of two AI laws

body.text: The Council is weighing a ban on selling or deploying AI in the five boroughs without outside-expert vetting, and a kill switch requirement, a human override that can shut down the system. Proposals only, not enacted.

caption:
Senior executives from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta testified under oath at a rare New York City Council hearing on AI risks on Oct 5, 2026. Elon Musk's SpaceXAI did not show up despite a subpoena, a legal order compelling attendance and sworn testimony.

The hearing convened all 51 Council members. The companies sent policy leads, not CEOs. Speaker Julie Menin's office says OpenAI, Google and Anthropic agreed to appear only after the Council threatened subpoenas. Menin says SpaceXAI's absence violates its subpoena and that the Council will pursue the matter in court. Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon called the industry's approach extremely reckless. The Council is weighing proposals that include outside-expert vetting of AI and a kill switch, with a $25,000 fine for violating either of those two laws. They are proposals only. Menin opened by criticising the federal government's light-touch approach.

Should a city be writing AI rules before the federal government does?
